cells.tense: You are standing in the open with enough light for the next step and no more.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been waiting to feel sure about, then take the smallest real step on it today, before the certainty arrives.
cells.core:
You can stand in the unclear and still move. Not because you've figured it out, but because what you've already been through is settled enough to trust. The dream you're carrying isn't a fantasy running ahead of your life. It's made of what you've actually lived, and that's why it has weight.

So the next step is available even without the whole road lit. You don't need to force a plan into shape or decide what it all means yet. Something is already moving, and what it wants from you is the small forward motion you can make today, one real step toward the thing you keep picturing. That's not pressure. That's the ground under you being solid enough to step from.
cells.sheetLine: You can move through the unclear because you've lived enough to trust your step.

cells.tense: You are living in a version of this that has not happened yet, and it is crowding out the one you are in.
cells.ask: Pick one scene you keep building in your head, set a timer for ten minutes, and write only what is true today.
cells.core:
The pictures have taken over the walking. There is a version where it all comes together, and you are spending your hours there — rearranging, imagining, rehearsing — while the ground you're actually on goes untended. The pictures feel like progress. They aren't yet.

What is absent is not vision. It is the patience to let a thing grow at its own speed. You don't have to kill the dream or force it into a schedule. Set it down for a day and let it stay a picture, not a blueprint. The small, regular, unglamorous care is what the future you're picturing gets built from. You can't hold it and grow it at the same time.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in the version that hasn't happened, and the real one is waiting.

cells.tense: You stopped leaning on the kind of knowing that arrives without argument, and you are still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Walk somewhere you don't usually go for ten minutes with no headphones, and notice which thing your attention keeps returning to.
cells.core:
There is a way of knowing that doesn't argue. It lands and you're already sure. You've quit leaning on it. These days everything has to come through reasoning or proof, and whatever arrives before that gets turned away at the door. That isn't skepticism. That's a door closed and left closed.

Nothing was lost. It just isn't being fed. Trying harder to feel something isn't the fix, and forcing depth where none is coming isn't either. Give your attention room to move on its own — no task, no output, no result to defend. Whatever it lands on is data. You don't have to call it anything. Just notice what it noticed.
cells.sheetLine: Something in you still picks up what matters before you say why.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what your life is pointing toward, and you describe it as something happening to you.
cells.ask: Write one sentence about what you're actually aiming at, stick it where you'll see it tomorrow, and don't edit it.
cells.core:
A picture of where this is going is steering your choices. Plenty of them only make sense in light of it. But you would call those same choices just getting through, or doing what's in front of you. The dream is running the show and getting no credit for it.

No one is asking you to announce a vision. But the thing guiding your decisions is already yours, and calling it outside you — luck, circumstance, what's needed right now — keeps you from working with it on purpose. A little regular attention to what you're actually aiming at does more than one big declaration. You don't have to be sure it's right. You just have to stop pretending you're not the one pointing.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person ever had a specific bad experience with intuition or depth, only that the capacity is currently under-expressed — the past-tense phrasing must locate the door without narrating what happened behind it. A reader could reasonably say 'I don't distrust intuition, I just don't have time for it' — the reading should survive that correction, so the ask must be a concrete act rather than a demand to feel something. The ask in each cell is a doable physical act (talking, walking, sitting down, writing) so it stays useful even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be any line that treats 'Potential' or 'Feedback' as something the person should recognize as their own vocabulary — those stay off the glass.
